investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T04:41–04:49Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not complete, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were never written, violating the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all concurrent or recently-created remote agent pods have claimed the available VM slots and none have been released, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new pods.

[Likely] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are under-provisioned relative to demand — the cluster was sized for a lower concurrency of remote agent pods than is currently being requested by the eval harness and/or real workloads.

[Possible] A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity became NotReady or was cordoned/drained between runs, reducing the eligible node pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes, both of which are now saturated.

[Possible] A previous eval run's cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) did not fully release the VM resource on the peer-pod nodes, leaving leaked VM allocations that are consuming the remaining capacity.

[Lower likelihood] The pod's node affinity/selector was recently tightened or the 4 non-kata nodes had labels changed, shrinking the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata nodes that are already saturated.

investigation.summary: The published observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 322 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the published-observability-snapshot check; all three sibling public-website checks passed, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 322 minutes old when the eval executed at 2026-06-20T04:49:09.747Z, causing the snapshotAgeMinutes assertion (max: 300, defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482) to fail. All other evidence fields passed their assertions, confirming the failure is exclusively a staleness issue with the upstream workflow publication cadence, not a structural or data-quality problem with the snapshot itself.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the live snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and passes it through statusSnapshotEvidence(), confirming the age value is derived directly from the published artifact, not a cached or synthetic value.
possibleCauses: Most likely — GitHub Actions snapshot-publication workflow skipped, failed, or was delayed: the evidence shows source='github-actions' and the snapshot is 322 minutes old, meaning the workflow did not complete a successful publish within the last 5 hours. A workflow failure, queue delay, or missed schedule trigger would produce exactly this result.

Secondary — GitHub Actions workflow ran but the published artifact (status.json on GitHub Pages) was not updated due to a Pages deployment lag, caching issue, or a failed push step after the workflow completed its computation.

Less likely — The snapshotAgeMinutes max threshold in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (300 minutes) is tighter than the registry staleAfterMinutes (360 minutes), creating a window where the snapshot is considered stale by the eval contract but not yet stale by the feature registry. If the workflow runs on a cadence near or beyond 300 minutes, transient scheduling drift could cause intermittent failures.
Least likely — A clock skew or timestamp computation error in the snapshot generation or in statusSnapshotEvidence() causing snapshotAgeMinutes to be reported as larger than the actual elapsed time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T04:41–04:49Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not complete, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were never written, violating the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
